text: NetDAO: Toward Trustful and Secure IoT Networks without Central Gateways should be assessed against Kaal's source-bound claim that A malicious party using Sybil accounts cannot be prevented from cloning the structure of a successful proof of stake blockchain at far lower cost than cloning a proof of work chain, leaving a new user unable to distinguish the truly decentralized chain from a clone that has manufactured even more tokens. The authors answer that this is resolved off chain, by a trusted user interface, as with cloned web pages. The current metadata indicates a plausible connection through decentralized autonomous organization, but the defensible response is a qualification until the source text confirms agreement, scope, methods, and limitations.
scope_conditions: new users joining without prior knowledge of the genuine chain
PoS chains where clone creation costs only new public keys
